review.reason:
The drawings do not support the measured numbers.

Reading. The boundary reading (alpha laths separated by thin bright beta ribs) is the physically right reading for a Ti-6Al-4V BSE image. At 720x, however, many laths are only a few pixels wide and the ribs are barely resolved. The outlines therefore mix two failures:
- long green and blue regions in the columnar prior-beta grains that clearly span several laths (merged across ribs);
- many short fragments, especially in the lower basketweave band (laths cut along their length).

The median aspect ratio of 2.16 is implausibly low for Widmanstätten/colony laths; I would expect several times higher. Because laths are both cut and merged, the per-flake numbers are not trustworthy. S = 0.39 is plausible for a multi-colony field, but I would not claim it is within tolerance. Prior-beta boundaries between columns are partly visible in the colour changes, but there are also merges across columns.

Masking.
- The bottom SEM data bar is filled with flake colours (red/teal at the WD/HV fields), so annotation text and boxes are being measured as flakes.
- The resin and mount edge at top and bottom are partly outlined.
- Coverage of 0.645 includes these areas.

Scratches. The header reports 0 scratches on the real image. I see no obvious scratch there, so this is fine. The white line in the centre appears to be the mean-direction arrow, not a scratch.

Twin.
- It is a periodic short-rod array with one straight scratch. It does not resemble the real image (correctly marked untrusted).
- The method also fails on the twin itself: flake recall 0.19, precision 0.11, aspect-ratio bias -57% (flakes cut short, consistent with the real image), and order-parameter error 0.23.
- Scratch recall across flakes is 0.15. The header says scratches0 even though a prominent bright scratch crosses the whole twin image and flakes are drawn across it.
- Worst family tolerance ratio is 7.5x.

History. The same set (distance 0) was already run with this reading and failed with essentially the same holdout score (7.48). The current tuning has not moved anything.

Confidence: high that the result should be rejected; moderate on the exact failure mix in the real image, given the low resolution.
review.next_step:
1) Fix masking before any tuning:
- exclude the SEM info bar (crop the bottom ~12% of rows, or add a data-bar detector: uniform dark band with text boxes);
- add a specimen mask that drops the near-black resin above and below the sample (threshold on local mean intensity, e.g. keep pixels above about 35% of the sample median), with a 5–10 px erosion at the sample edge.

2) Address resolution. Laths are about 2–4 px wide, so upsample the real image 2x before ridge detection. Halve the boundary ridge scale accordingly (ridge sigma about 1.5 px -> 0.75 px at native size, or keep the sigma and upsample). Lower the minimum ridge contrast so the faint beta ribs separate the long merged laths. Raise the gap-closing length along the lath direction, and stop splitting on short gaps or across the lath (oriented closing aligned with the local orientation field), to stop fragmentation. Watch whether the median aspect ratio rises from about 2 towards a believable value; check this only on the real drawings plus the rotation test.

3) Scratch detector. It misses a full-width bright straight line on the twin (recall 0.15). Lower the scratch minimum line contrast, lower the required straightness or min length so that a line spanning about 70% of the image width qualifies, and make sure it runs before flake segmentation so flakes are not merged or cut across it.

4) Replace the twin generator for this set: long, thin alpha laths in colonies and basketweave, inside columnar prior-beta grains, with thin bright beta ribs, BSE-like noise, and lath widths of 2–4 px. Until a trusted twin exists, the tolerance claims cannot be checked.

If, after the upsampling and masking changes, laths are still merged across ribs, then no parameter of the boundary reading can resolve laths at this magnification. The honest outcome is to report only image-level direction and S, from a structure-tensor orientation field, and drop per-flake aspect ratio and misalignment for this set.

review.reason:
The real image looks like a back-scattered electron image of TiAl lamellae. Its lamellae differ from one another by steps between several grey levels (white, light grey, dark grey, near black), and there are no thin dark lines between them. That is the regions reading, not the boundary reading. Same-set history agrees: tial_lamellar_L26, at distance 0.0, already failed with the boundary reading.

What the drawing shows on the real image:
(a) Neighbouring lamellae of similar grey merge into wide blocks. Examples are the broad blue and purple patches at top right and the wide teal and blue strips at bottom centre. In the micrograph these hold several thin lamellae each.
(b) Long lamellae are broken into short pieces wherever their grey level drifts. The reported median aspect ratio of 3.28 is far below what the micrograph shows: lamellae there run for hundreds of pixels at widths of a few pixels, so their aspect ratios look to be well above 10. This low value matches the twin's aspect-ratio bias of -43%.
(c) The large blocky grey areas (equiaxed gamma, or wide single-tone regions) are mostly set aside correctly. Some are coloured, though, which suggests they enter the statistics.
(d) Colony-level orientation colours do follow the visible colonies roughly: magenta top centre, cyan and blue in the lower half, yellow right. So the mean direction may be only loosely right. Per-flake counts (n = 5084), aspect ratio, S = 0.57 and coverage 0.68 are not supported by the drawing.
(e) Scratches: I cannot identify any scratch overlay on the real image. The one white line in the magenta colony is the mean-direction arrow.

The twin is untrusted and does not resemble the real image. It shows dark rounded rods in a light matrix with dots, a phase-in-matrix structure. Its scores add to the doubt rather than settling anything:
- flake precision is 0.23, because the matrix bands between rods are coloured as flakes;
- aspect-ratio bias is -0.43;
- worst tolerance ratio is 2.88;
- the header reads scratches0, yet obvious scratches are present and scratch recall is 0.66.

Confidence: about 75% that the reading is wrong and the per-flake numbers are not supported; high confidence that the result cannot be accepted as it stands.
review.next_step:
1. Change reading: boundaries -> regions. Split flakes at grey-level steps between neighbouring lamellae rather than at thin lines.
2. Regenerate the twin to resemble this set before tuning against it: switch the twin generator from phase-in-matrix rods to colonies of parallel lamellae in 3–4 grey levels, with no lines between lamellae, widths of about 3–20 px, plus blocky equiaxed regions and occasional scratches. Then check that the twin becomes trusted.
3. After that, tune the grey-step threshold that separates neighbouring lamellae and the minimum flake width, aiming to raise the median aspect ratio and cut the merged blocks.
4. Re-run the rotation self-consistency check on the real image.

If the regions reading still cannot resolve the finest lamellae, which are only a few px wide, state plainly that per-flake aspect ratio and counts are out of reach at this resolution. In that case report only colony-level direction and order parameter.

review.reason:
Reading: the dark lenticular plates in bright ferrite are what a metallographer would measure. Most coloured fills lie on those plates, which run at about 30°, and the bright ferrite stays unfilled. So the phase reading with the dark phase is right (about 75% confident). One inconsistency should be checked: the two-scale report labels the flake phase 'bright' (area share 0.35), which conflicts with the stated dark-phase reading.

Where the drawing fails on the real image:
(1) Plates are cut along their length. Many long yellow and green plates are split by cross-cuts into 2–4 segments, and short orange or red stubs sit at the plate tips. This is why the median aspect ratio is 2.08, while visible plates have length-to-width ratios of roughly 8–15. The reported AR is therefore not supported.
(2) Non-plate dark material is taken as flakes. The broad dark band at lower centre is filled with large blocky green, yellow and purple patches. The dark, mottled region along the top edge (dislocation contrast and the upper grain) is broken into dozens of small irregular, multicoloured blobs that are coloured, so they are counted. They should be grey (excluded) or left unsegmented. These blobs add random orientations, so the order parameter S = 0.80 is probably biased low, and the 304 'used' flakes are inflated.
(3) A false scratch: a white scratch line is drawn in the centre, parallel to the plates. A TEM foil has no polishing scratches, so this is a false positive. It may also be cutting or merging plates where it lies.
(4) The mean direction (about 30°) and the colony-level colouring look right.

Twin: it scores well, but its plates are uniform rounded rods in tidy colonies. It has no tapered lenticular plates, no mottled dislocation-contrast regions and no wide dark bands, so its good AR error (2.6%) does not carry over to this image. Its scratch recall on crossings is 0.31, so scratch handling is weak anyway.

Confidence that the measured AR and the flake count are wrong: high. Confidence that the direction is right: moderate-high.
review.next_step:
Keep the dark-phase reading. Parameter names below are generic, because the method's exact names were not given; map them to the matching settings.
1. Reduce lengthwise splitting: raise the split/watershed threshold, e.g. watershed_h or split_min_neck 1 -> 3 px. Enable merging of collinear fragments with orientation difference under 10° and an end gap under 1.5× plate width.
2. Exclude blocky dark regions from the statistics: raise min_aspect_ratio_used 1.5 -> 2.5. Add a local-texture or solidity filter, e.g. solidity_min 0.0 -> 0.8, so the mottled top region and the wide dark band turn grey. Set max_width_px to about 2× the fine scale (about 50 px).
3. Turn off scratch detection for TEM images, or raise scratch_min_length and scratch_min_contrast so that features parallel to the plates are not flagged.
4. Regenerate the twin with tapered lenticular plates that vary in width, plus mottled dark regions, before trusting its AR scores.
5. Resolve the bright/dark flag mismatch in the scale report.
6. Then run the rotation self-consistency check again and recheck that the median AR rises above about 5.

review.reason:
Phase reading is correct for this image: the long bright primary-cementite needles in the ledeburite matrix are the flakes. The coloured regions in the drawing do lie on those bright needles. That contradicts the stated 'flakes are the dark phase', so the polarity setting needs checking.

The drawings do not support the numbers:
(1) Long needles are cut along their length into several pieces, and the pieces sometimes get different colours. This happens mostly where needles cross each other, e.g. top-right orange/purple needles and the centre yellow/magenta pair.
(2) Many clearly visible needles stay grey, so they are not used. Coverage is only 0.19, and several near-horizontal needles in the left half are missing.
(3) Many small coloured specks in the eutectic/ledeburite regions are matrix lamellae taken as flakes. They make up much of n=359 and pull the median aspect ratio down to 2.1, whereas the visible needles have aspect ratios of roughly 15–50. The aspect-ratio figure is wrong by about an order of magnitude.
S=0.21 (near-random needle network) is plausible, but its value is uncertain given the contamination. No scratches are visible, and none were reported. Colony/grain boundaries are not the issue here; crossings between needles are.

The twin is useless as evidence. Its short-dash colonies do not resemble crossing needles. Flake recall is 0, its drawing shows dashes merged into large grey blobs, and it is untrusted.

The closest prior set, needles_L23 (distance 0, same reading), also failed: rotation check 0.70, holdout worst family 4.2. Repeating that configuration will not succeed.

Confidence: high that this should be rejected; moderate on the exact causes.
review.next_step:
Parameter names below are illustrative; map them to the method's actual names.
(a) Set flake polarity: dark -> bright, so the stated reading matches what is segmented.
(b) Raise min_flake_area by about 5–10x, to roughly the area of a needle 3 widths long, and require minimum aspect ratio for use 1.5 -> 4. This drops the ledeburite specks.
(c) Split at crossings by orientation rather than merging or fragmenting there: enable skeleton/branch splitting with an angle threshold of about 15°, and re-join collinear fragments across gaps of up to 2 needle widths (merge_collinear: off -> on, max_angle 10°).
(d) Regenerate the twin as long, straight, randomly oriented crossing needles (width 5–20 px, length 200–1500 px) on a fine eutectic-textured matrix, and do not score until it is trusted.
If (b) and (c) cannot both keep crossing needles separate and remove matrix fragments, state that the current method cannot measure needle aspect ratios on this set.

review.reason:
Reading (confidence about 0.7): the regions reading fits the real image. It is a BSE-type TiAl/Ti lamellar micrograph in which strips of 3–4 grey levels touch without dark separating lines. The drawing colours the colonies coherently: steep cyan/blue in the lower half, magenta/purple diagonal in the upper middle, orange/green in the right, with grey for the equiaxed dark patches at top right. The mean direction and the colony split are therefore plausible.

The drawings do not support the numbers, for three reasons.

(1) Twin, which is the only place with truth: worst tolerance ratio is 1.97 and worst family 2.56, both above 1. Flake recall is only 0.55. Aspect ratio has a +29% bias, and the bias equals the relative error, so it is systematic overestimation. The twin drawing shows why. Adjacent same-orientation flakes are merged into blobs, e.g. the magenta/purple H-shaped region centre-left and grey merged clumps along the colony boundaries. Collinear flakes are also joined end to end. Both raise the aspect ratio and lower recall.

(2) Scratches: the header says scratches0, and none of the three bright scratches is drawn as a white line. Instead they are segmented as thin orange/red flakes, and they cut the lamellae they cross. The listed scratch precision 0.95 / recall 0.90 cannot belong to this drawing. Either the scores are from a different configuration or split, or the drawing is wrong. This must be resolved before any score is trusted.

(3) Real image: no scratches are visible, so that part cannot be checked. In the fine-lamella band at the bottom (fine width about 18 px against coarse about 79 px), the coloured strips look wider than the individual white/black lamellae in the micrograph. I am unsure at this resolution, but it suggests neighbouring fine lamellae are merged, which would inflate AR (4.37) and lower S. Several large white equiaxed patches on the left are coloured as flakes rather than grey, so possible grain-boundary/globular alpha is taken as flakes. Coverage is 0.67.

No rotation check is reported for this regions configuration. The earlier 0.974 was for the boundary reading on L26. The twin is untrusted, so even a pass there would say little about this image.

Confidence the result is not acceptable: about 0.85.
review.next_step:
Keep the regions reading. Parameter names below are generic, since the method's exact names are not given here; map them to the actual params.

1. Explain the scratch contradiction first: check whether the scratch detector ran on this image (header scratches0 vs recall 0.90).
2. Scratch detection: scratch_min_length 0.25×image -> 0.15×image; scratch_ridge_threshold lowered by about 30%; scratch_max_width about 8 px; scratch_orientation_deviation_from_local_lamellae 20° -> 10°, so straight bright lines oblique to the colony are flagged and cut out before region merging.
3. Under-splitting: grey-level step threshold for region splitting (region_merge_delta) lowered by one quantisation level, e.g. 0.08 -> 0.05 of the intensity range; collinear-merge / end-joining off; max flake length cap tied to colony size.
4. Two scales: run with flake_width_scale set per region (about 18 px in the fine band, about 79 px elsewhere), or use multi_scale: true instead of a single scale.
5. Grain-boundary/globular alpha: exclude regions with aspect ratio < 2 or solidity < 0.8 from the orientation set (grey).
6. Rerun the dev twin and require worst ratio < 1 and AR bias < 10%.
7. Run the rotation self-consistency check (90° and an arbitrary angle) on the real image for this configuration before the next review.

If the twin stays untrusted, regenerate it with BSE-like multi-level touching lamellae and fine/coarse bands matching 18/79 px, so its scores say something about this set.

review.reason: Reading: in this BSE image of Ti-6Al-4V the alpha laths are the mid-grey bands and the beta is the thin bright ribs between them. The boundary reading (flakes between thin lines) therefore outlines roughly the right objects, and the coarse colour field follows the colonies: blue/cyan near-vertical laths in the upper V-shaped colonies, orange/red/magenta near-horizontal laths in the finer lower band. Confidence in the reading is moderate (~65%); a phase reading with bright beta as the matrix would outline nearly the same laths. The numbers are not supported, for four reasons. (1) The laths are cut along their length. The upper colonies hold laths hundreds of px long and a few px wide, yet the median aspect ratio is 2.1, and the drawing shows long laths broken into short segments. The twin confirms this as a systematic bias: aspect-ratio bias -0.58, flake recall 0.22, flake precision 0.10, and the twin drawing shows each lamella chopped into short blobs (AR 1.7). (2) Coverage is only 0.66. Many grey (unused) regions sit inside clean colonies, especially in the lower fine band, so S=0.41 and the local S come from a biased subset. I cannot judge from the drawing whether 0.41 is right; it is plausible for a multi-colony field but not verified. (3) Scratches: the real image shows no visible scratch and none is drawn; the vertical white line at about x=1175 is the mean-direction arrow (88°), not a scratch. On the twin, the obvious diagonal bright scratch was missed (scratches 0, crossing recall 0.0), so scratch handling is untested at best. (4) The twin is untrusted: it is a periodic single-orientation pattern with beads and does not resemble this multi-colony basketweave structure. Its worst family tolerance ratio of about 8 says the method fails even on easy synthetic data, but it cannot certify the real image. The prior identical set (sem_user) also failed, with a rotation check of 0.45. Colony boundaries do appear as colour changes, but given the fragmentation the per-flake orientation, misalignment and aspect ratio cannot be trusted. The evidence does not support any of the measured numbers within tolerance.
review.next_step: Keep the boundary reading and stop the cutting along the lath length. (a) Smooth along the local orientation before boundary detection: orientation/structure-tensor sigma ~1.5 -> ~3 px, with anisotropic smoothing elongated along the lath (aspect ~3:1). (b) Raise the boundary-line contrast threshold, e.g. 1 SD -> ~1.5-2 SD above the local background, so intensity variation inside a lath is not taken as a boundary. (c) Merge fragments that are collinear and share a short boundary when their orientations differ by < ~10°, but never merge across a colony boundary (orientation jump > ~20°). (d) Raise the minimum flake area, e.g. 20 -> ~40 px, so fragments are not counted as used flakes. (e) Scratches: lower the line-detector threshold and require length > ~5x the median lath length, plus straightness over many colonies, so the twin's diagonal scratch is found; then check that it splits no flakes. (f) Rebuild the twin to match this set before trusting any score: multiple colonies with V/herringbone arrangement, bright thin beta ribs, lath width ~3-6 px, AR ~8-15, and a finer near-horizontal band at the bottom. Then rerun the rotation check (target well above 0.45). If aspect ratio stays near 2 after (a)-(d), the method's line detector cannot resolve these thin beta ribs at 720x; report that no parameter of this method fixes it, and test a regions/phase reading on bright beta as the matrix instead.
